part.text:
I have all the evidence needed. Here is my answer.

## Answer: Yes

curl **can** print transfer stats as JSON with `-w/--write-out`, via `-w "%{json}"` (the `%{json}` variable outputs a JSON object containing all available write-out keys).

## Supporting commit

**`04c03416e68fd635a15cae8201872f5c29fdcca8`** — "writeout: support to generate JSON output"
- Author: Mathias Gumz
- Committed: 2020-03-17 (by Daniel Stenberg), Closes #4870

### Evidence from the commit message

> ```
> writeout: support to generate JSON output
>
> This commit adds support to generate JSON via the writeout feature:
>
>     -w "%{json}"
>
> It leverages the existing infrastructure as much as possible. Thus,
> generating the JSON on STDERR is possible by:
>
>     -w "%{stderr}%{json}"
> ```

### Evidence from the diff

The docs (`docs/cmdline-opts/write-out.d`) add the new `json` variable:

```diff
 .TP
+.B json
+A JSON object with all available keys.
+.TP
 .B local_ip
```

The implementation (`src/tool_writeout.c`) adds the variable and its dispatch:

```diff
+  {"json", VAR_JSON, 1,
+   0, JSON_NONE},
+  {NULL, VAR_NONE, 1,
+   0, JSON_NONE}
...
               case VAR_STDERR:
                 stream = stderr;
                 break;
+              case VAR_JSON:
+                ourWriteOutJSON(variables, curl, outs, stream);
               default:
                 break;
```

plus new files `src/tool_writeout_json.c` / `src/tool_writeout_json.h` (the JSON serializer) wired into `src/Makefile.inc`.

### Related history (for context)

- `4133a69f2` ("curl: add %{header_json} support in -w handling", 2022-03-22) later added `%{header_json}` for outputting response headers as a JSON object.
- `65ca229` (2021-02-09) refactored write-out and JSON write-out into shared code.

No files were modified; this was a read-only investigation.
